provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Standing and sleeping lines
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify standing lines.
The pupils should be able to trace sleeping lines.
Introduction:
Last week we learned how to hold our pencils.
Today we will draw straight lines.
Content:
Standing lines go up and down like a tree.
Sleeping lines go left to right like a bed.
We trace with our fingers first.
Then we use pencils on paper.
Class activity:
Children stand up and make standing lines with their arms.
Then they lie down on mats to make sleeping lines.
Evaluation questions:
Show me a standing line.
Draw a sleeping line.
Which line looks like a flagpole?
Summary:
We can draw both standing and sleeping lines.

topics.title: Tracing patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to trace zigzag lines.
The pupils should be able to trace wavy lines.
Introduction:
Last week we learned straight lines.
Today we will learn fun lines.
Content:
Zigzag lines go up and down like mountains.
Wavy lines go up and down like water.
Curves bend like a rainbow.
We trace from left to right.
Class activity:
Children use their fingers in sand to make patterns.
Then they trace with crayons on paper.
Evaluation questions:
Draw a zigzag line.
Show me a wavy line.
Which pattern looks like a snake?
Summary:
We can make many different patterns.

topics.title: Tracing circles
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw circles in the air.
The pupils should be able to trace big circles.
Introduction:
Last week we learned pattern lines.
Today we will learn round shapes.
Content:
A circle is round like a wheel.
We draw circles in the air with our fingers.
We trace big circles on paper.
Then we colour inside the circle.
Class activity:
Children make circles with their bodies.
They use hula hoops to walk around.
Evaluation questions:
Show me a circle.
Draw a circle in the air.
What is round like a circle?
Summary:
Circles are round and fun to draw.

topics.title: Letter Aa
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of A.
The pupils should be able to trace capital A.
The pupils should be able to trace small a.
Introduction:
Last week we learned circles.
Today we will learn letter A.
Content:
A sounds like apple.
Capital A has two slanting lines and one cross line.
Small a is like a circle with a tail.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children say A sound while clapping.
They trace A in sand with their fingers.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does A make?
Trace capital A.
Draw small a in the air.
Summary:
Letter A makes the sound of apple.

topics.title: Letter Bb
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of B.
The pupils should be able to trace capital B.
The pupils should be able to trace small b.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter A.
Today we will learn letter B.
Content:
B sounds like ball.
Capital B has a straight line and two bumps.
Small b has a straight line and a bump below.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children bounce balls while saying B sound.
They trace B with chalk on the board.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does B make?
Trace capital B.
Draw small b on paper.
Summary:
Letter B makes the sound of ball.

topics.title: Letter Cc
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of C.
The pupils should be able to trace capital C.
The pupils should be able to trace small c.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter B.
Today we will learn letter C.
Content:
C sounds like cat.
Capital C is like a half circle.
Small c is like a smaller half circle.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children make C shape with their bodies.
They trace C with paint on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does C make?
Trace capital C.
Draw small c in the sand.
Summary:
Letter C makes the sound of cat.

topics.title: Letter Dd
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of D.
The pupils should be able to trace capital D.
The pupils should be able to trace small d.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter C.
Today we will learn letter D.
Content:
D sounds like drum.
Capital D has a straight line and a bump.
Small d has a small circle and a straight line.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children pretend to play drums while saying D sound.
They trace D with sticks in sand.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does D make?
Trace capital D.
Draw small d on paper.
Summary:
Letter D makes the sound of drum.

topics.title: Letter Ee
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of E.
The pupils should be able to trace capital E.
The pupils should be able to trace small e.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter D.
Today we will learn letter E.
Content:
E sounds like egg.
Capital E has one straight line and three cross lines.
Small e has a circle and a straight line.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children make E shape with their arms.
They trace E with crayons on paper.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does E make?
Trace capital E.
Draw small e in the air.
Summary:
Letter E makes the sound of egg.

topics.title: Letter Ff
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of F.
The pupils should be able to trace capital F.
The pupils should be able to trace small f.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter E.
Today we will learn letter F.
Content:
F sounds like fan.
Capital F has one straight line and two cross lines.
Small f has a long straight line and a short cross line.
We trace from top to bottom.
Class activity:
Children pretend to use a fan while saying F sound.
They trace F with chalk on the board.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does F make?
Trace capital F.
Draw small f on paper.
Summary:
Letter F makes the sound of fan.

topics.title: Revision and colouring fun
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say sounds A to F.
The pupils should be able to match letters to pictures.
The pupils should be able to colour letters.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter F.
Today we will revise all letters.
Content:
We say the sounds of A B C D E F.
We match letters to pictures that start with those sounds.
We colour the letters we learned.
Class activity:
Children play a letter sound game.
They colour their favorite letter.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does A make?
Match B to ball.
Colour letter C.
Which letter is your favorite?
Summary:
We can say all sounds and colour letters.
